# Koraṇḍiyajātaka (Ja 356)

**ID:** Ja 356
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Koraṇḍiyajātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Koraṇḍiyajātaka* (Ja 356), also titled *The Student Koraṇḍiya* and attested in edition variants as the *Kārandiyajātaka*, is a story in the Pali Jātaka collection [Fausböll 1883]. In its framing narrative set at Jetavana, the Buddha relates the story concerning the "Captain of the Faith," the elder Sāriputta. The elder was accustomed to preaching the moral law to unvirtuous people such as hunters and fishermen, who accepted the law out of respect for him but were unable to observe it and returned to their occupations. In the conclusion (*samodhāna*) of the Jātaka, the Buddha explains that Sāriputta was the teacher (brāhmaṇa) of that past lifetime, while the Bodhisatta was the pupil Koraṇḍiya (Kāraṇḍiyamāṇava) [Fausböll 1883].

**Sources**
